paragraphs.text: Abstract. An Al-0.5Mg-0.4Si alloy was processed by equal-channel angular pressing for four passes at room temperature, producing an ultrafine-grained microstructure with a mean grain size of 480 nm.

Tensile tests at an initial strain rate of 1e-3 per s gave an ultimate tensile strength of 385 MPa and an elongation to failure of 14.2 percent, compared with 312 MPa and 21.5 percent for the coarse-grained counterpart.
Microhardness increased from 92 HV in the as-received state to 128 HV after four passes, following the profile of the imposed strain.
The strength-ductility trade-off is interpreted by the authors as a consequence of reduced dislocation storage capacity in ultrafine grains; texture effects were not separately deconvoluted.
Corrosion performance in 3.5 wt percent NaCl solution was not tested and remains an open question for service applications.
